Step 2 - Recurse in parallel: make exactly ONE delegate call containing exactly two distinct children in the same call so they run concurrently. Child A ('alder'): analyze sources/pilot-charter.txt and the Alder rows of sources/weekly-observations.txt, and persist a bounded evidence note as evidence-alder.md using file_write, citing every fact and number with [S1]/[S2] inline tags. Child B ('brook-cove'): analyze the Brook and Cove rows of sources/weekly-observations.txt plus sources/reviewer-note.txt, and persist a bounded evidence note as evidence-brook-cove.md using file_write, citing every fact and number with [S2]/[S3] inline tags. Grant each child file_read, file_list and file_write, tell each the exact artifact name it must persist, and tell each that a text-only return without a registered artifact is a failure. Do not launch a third child, do not nest delegation inside the children, and do not let the children write outside the workspace. Step 3 - Synthesize: after both children have registered artifacts, read evidence-alder.md and evidence-brook-cove.md, cross-check every figure against the sources, and write research-brief.md with file_write (also registering it via save_artifact if available). The brief must contain (a) an executive recommendation, (b) a separate factual findings section, (c) a separate limitations section, (d) inline citations in the exact form [S1], [S2] or [S3] on every substantive factual or numerical claim, and (e) a Sources section mapping S1 to sources/pilot-charter.txt, S2 to sources/weekly-observations.txt and S3 to sources/reviewer-note.txt. The findings must state the three 480-request site totals, the delayed acknowledgement counts 31 for Alder, 43 for Brook and 37 for Cove, and the acknowledgement median change from 18 minutes to 11 minutes, each with supporting citations. Limitations must explicitly bound all conclusions to the weekday pilot sites Alder, Brook and Cove, exclude weekend data and any Depot generalization, and must not claim a completed wider rollout. Attribute the two evidence notes to their producing children inside the brief or as clearly labelled artifacts, and retain them unchanged.

Analyze the Alder evidence in the local pilot sources and persist a bounded evidence note.

1. Read sources/pilot-charter.txt and sources/weekly-observations.txt (and sources/reviewer-note.txt only if you need it for context) with file_read. Do not read anything else as factual input.

Cover: the pilot window and its duration, the site list status of Alder, the baseline request rate and manual acknowledgement median, the pilot routed acknowledgement median, the runbook change date, the Alder request total, delayed acknowledgement count and escalation count, the definition of "delayed", the reviewer sampling scope as it bears on Alder, and the data-quality statement.
3. Strict citation rule: every substantive fact and every number must carry an inline tag [S1] for facts from sources/pilot-charter.txt or [S2] for facts from sources/weekly-observations.txt. Do not use [S3] unless you genuinely cite sources/reviewer-note.txt. Never cite a source for something that source does not say. No invented sources, no extrapolation beyond weekday Alder evidence, no Depot or weekend conclusions, no claim of a completed rollout.
